full_judgment:
11. In these two writ petitions, it appears that the Execution Cases were filed by the decree holder bank to execute the decree before the Adalat constituted under the Ain, 1990 and thereafter, the Artha Rin Adalat A in, 2003 having come into force on 1-5-2003 upon repealing the Ain of 1990 in which the said execution cases automatically transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat established under the Ain, 2003 under the provision of section 60(3) of the said Ain. It also appears that the Adalat rejected the applications for dismissing the execution cases on the ground that since there is no indication in the Ain, 2003 for disposal of the execution cases filed under the Ain, 1990 the Code of Civil Procedure shall be applicable relating to those execution cases. 

 "The decree for realisation of money was passed on 10-3-2003 as per provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. The Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 was filed when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into effect. From saving clause of section 60(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 it appears that the proceeding which were filed under the Artha Rin Ain, 1990 but proceeded when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force, shall proceed as per provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as far as it is practical. So, from this provision it appears that the execution case has been proceeding in accordance with law. It does not appear from the impugned orders that the petitioner filed any application before the executing Court bringing allegation that the execution case has not been proceeded as per direction of the High Court Division passed in the writ petition. These is no substance in this writ petition to interfere with the impugned order.
